label: Parity: a feature-uniform demand for a reason why excludes a brute contingent truth
meaning: The owner's parity argument, analyst formulation, attribution deferred. The stance requires a reason why the target exists (P1), its demand is uniform in a feature k (P3) on which the target and the accepted fact o agree (P2). So it requires a reason why o obtains. If it met its demand and accepted o, o would have a reason, so it is not a brute contingent truth. For the naturalist who rejects an unreasoned God, God's existence as a mere brute fact in the owner's wording (target God, o the contingent foundation) it excludes the brute-contingency rival; the same theorem binds a theist who rejects brute contingents and is uniform in the reason status (target a contingent existent, o God's existence), so the demand is symmetric and leaves the comparative question which side's explanation of existence leaves less unexplained (parity map). It establishes neither B2 nor that anything has a reason, it does not answer whether there is evidence for God, and it binds only stances that hold P1, P2 and P3 for one feature.
